content.comment_body: The maximum value you can use in a mathematical instruction is 32,767. I'm tracking the daily liters of gas, but my total can exceed this limit. My idea is to have the first counter (Hundreds Counter) count up to 1000, then increment the second counter (Thousands counter) by 1 and reset the first counter. In my current setup, the program simulates 25 liters per minute when A1 is set to 1000, though the rate changes if A1 is lowered. I would like the Hundreds counter to increase by the sum of B003 and the previous count each minute, accumulating until it reaches 1000, then incrementing the Thousands counter by 1 and resetting the Hundreds counter to zero. The Thousands counter would continue incrementing up to 32,767. Does anyone have suggestions for designing a program to achieve this functionality? Thank you.
You mentioned hours counters earlier, but now you are talking about up/down counters? I'm having trouble following your reasoning.
Apologies, I intended this as a separate topic. Thank you for your support.

Closed because the question was posted twice. The duplicate topic titled 'Help overcoming the maximum number limitation in an LSC mathematical instruction' has already been published in the conference related to [product_name] software. Best regards, [user_name]
